newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean state bank to bail out Kia Steel.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean state bank to bail out Kia Steel.

text.p: South Korea's state-run Korea Development Bank (KDB) said on Wednesday it would extend 30 billion won ($33.8 million) in emergency loans to debt-stricken Kia Steel, a unit of the Kia Group.
"The company will be able to get the loans from this week," an official at the bank said. There were no further details.

The bank said on Monday that two Kia affiliates -- Kia Steel and Kia Motors -- were seeking loans of 30 billion won each. Kia group has also confirmed it was seeking government help to keep credit lines open.
KDB said Kia Steel had asked for the loans to meet its operating expenses, while group flagship Kia Motors needed funds to finance investment.

The country's eighth-largest conglomerate has been rumoured to be in financial trouble for months, speculation denied by the company, and commercial banks have shied away from extending credit. The government has also said the KIA group was a sound company.

Kia Steel's debts mounted after heavy investment in expansion of a steel bar plant, reaching about 1.3 trillion won at the end of 1996. This compares with its shareholders' equity of 47.4 billion won.

Company officials have said Kia affiliates would restructure, and on Tuesday the group's senior managing director Oh Min-boo warned that a growing reluctance by financial institutions to extend credits was damaging the nation's industrial competitiveness.

The group's shares have taken a beating since early June when a report leaked by Samsung Motors alleged "managerial conflicts" at flagship Kia Motors and hinted of a takeover. Kia Motors has denied the report.
Korea's financial community is nervous because of the collapse of two other steel companies -- Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel Co -- in March.
The Samsung report exacerbated Kia's difficulties because it suggested the nation's crowded car industry must be restructured to survive. ($1 = 887 won)
